tagline: Home of Luang Pho Sothon on the Bang Pakong River, an easy trip from Bangkok with old markets, big temples, and mango orchards
introHtml:
Chachoengsao, which locals usually just call Paet Riu, sits east of Bangkok. Drive out past Min Buri or hop on the eastern train line and you're there in no time. The first thing people picture is Luang Pho Sothon at Wat Sothon Wararam, the revered Buddha image that draws people coming to pray for good fortune all year round. It's a riverside town on the Bang Pakong, where you can still see old wooden houses and life along the water.

Beyond the temples there's the century-old Ban Mai Market, a riverside row of old wooden shophouses where you can eat your way through the day. Wat Saman Rattanaram has a huge reclining Ganesha, and Wat Hong Thong sits right on the coast, stretching out into the bay. Chachoengsao is mango country too, and in fruit season the orchards fill with nam dok mai and kaeo mangoes. Bangkok folks often drive out to pray, walk the markets, and eat noodles and riverside food on a quick day trip.
bestTime: November–February is cool and comfortable, good for walking the markets and visiting temples all day. March–May is mango season, when you can stop by the orchards and buy fresh fruit straight off the trees.

highlights.name: Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan (Luang Pho Sothon)
highlights.blurb: The town's signature temple on the Bang Pakong River, home to Luang Pho Sothon, a sacred Buddha image that draws people praying for blessings all year round.

highlights.name: Ban Mai Hundred-Year Market
highlights.blurb: A riverside market of old wooden shophouses nearly a century old, where you can eat noodles, traditional sweets, and good riverside food all day. It's the spot people think of when they mention Paet Riu.

highlights.name: Wat Saman Rattanaram
highlights.blurb: A temple on the Bang Pakong River with a huge pink reclining Ganesha, one of the province's most popular spots for paying respects and taking photos.

highlights.name: Bang Pakong River
highlights.blurb: The main river running through the heart of the province, with riverside life, old wooden houses, and dolphin-watching boat trips at the river mouth from late in the year into early the next.

highlights.name: Wat Hong Thong
highlights.blurb: A coastal temple with a walkway and a chedi set out over the water, reaching into the bay. You can stroll out for the sea breeze and feed the fish. It's around Bang Pakong district.

highlights.name: Paet Riu Mango Orchards
highlights.blurb: Chachoengsao is mango country, and in fruit season the orchards fill with nam dok mai and kaeo mangoes. Stop by to buy them fresh off the trees to take home.

foodScene.name: Riverside noodles at Ban Mai Market
foodScene.note: The century-old Ban Mai Market has several long-running noodle shops where you eat by the water in old wooden shophouses. It's a meal anyone visiting Paet Riu should try.

foodScene.name: Paet Riu mangoes
foodScene.note: The province's signature fruit, including nam dok mai, kaeo, and khiao sawoei mangoes. They ripen around March–May. Buy them fresh or as preserves like dried mango paste and candied mango.

foodScene.name: Khanom pia and traditional sweets
foodScene.note: The old markets and souvenir shops in town carry khanom pia, old-style Thai sweets, and traditional snacks to take home.

foodScene.name: Seafood from the Bang Pakong river mouth
foodScene.note: Around Bang Pakong and the coast there are seafood spots serving prawns, shellfish, crab, and fresh fish from the river mouth. You can eat by the water in the breeze.

foodScene.name: Mu yo and preserved snacks
foodScene.note: In town there are shops selling mu yo, Chinese sausage, and dried goods to take home alongside the mangoes.

foodScene.name: Mu krata
foodScene.note: A popular dinner with locals and groups of friends, with plenty of easygoing, well-priced spots to choose from.

foodScene.name: Riverside and in-town cafes
foodScene.note: Along the Bang Pakong River and around town there are cafes with water views and newly opened coffee shops, good for a break between temple visits and market walks.

attractions.name: Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan
attractions.blurb: The temple housing Luang Pho Sothon, a sacred Buddha image on the Bang Pakong River and a must-stop for praying when you visit Paet Riu.

attractions.name: Ban Mai Hundred-Year Market
attractions.blurb: A riverside market of old wooden shophouses nearly a century old, where you walk for good food and soak up the atmosphere of the old quarter along the river.

attractions.name: Wat Saman Rattanaram
attractions.blurb: A temple on the Bang Pakong River with a huge pink reclining Ganesha, a popular spot for paying respects and taking photos.

attractions.name: Wat Hong Thong
attractions.blurb: A coastal temple around Bang Pakong with a walkway and a chedi out over the water, reaching into the bay. You can stroll out for the sea breeze and feed the fish.

attractions.name: Dolphin-watching boat trip at the Bang Pakong river mouth
attractions.blurb: From late in the year into early the next there are boat trips out to the Bang Pakong river mouth to see pods of Irrawaddy dolphins, a standout nature activity in the province.

attractions.name: Khao Din Wang Tan
attractions.blurb: A low-hill area around Phanom Sarakham district with viewpoints over the rice fields and orchards, good for stopping to take photos and catch the breeze.

attractions.name: Wat Khao Din (Wildlife Sanctuary)
attractions.blurb: An area of forest and natural wildlife near the provincial border, with big shady trees and spots for walking and taking in nature.

attractions.name: Old town and markets in Chachoengsao city
attractions.blurb: In town there are markets, local food shops, and old houses along the river, where you can taste your way around and pick up souvenirs before heading back.

itineraryIdeas: Chachoengsao 1 day — pray to Luang Pho Sothon and walk Ban Mai Market
Chachoengsao temple run — Sothon, Saman Rattanaram, Hong Thong
